newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates steady as banks hold back.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates steady as banks hold back.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates were steady at an average of 10.53125 percent as banks adopted a wait-and-see attitude on the direction of interest rates, traders said.
Rates were still locked in the range of 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent, with 18 lenders and 15 borrowers.
Market volume was higher at 8.820 billion from 7.224 billion pesos.
"Banks want to hold on to their money," a big bank dealer said, despite the high liquidity in the market.
Banks expect Treasury bill rates to rally at Monday's auction after steep declines the past two weeks triggered by a reserve requirement cut.

With the Central Bank remaining firm at its overnight borrowing rate at 10.5 percent, rates are not going to drop further, dealers said. A further slide in rates would cause peso speculation, they said.
In anticipation that rates may have bottomed out, the secondary market of T-bills was swamped with many sellers.
Banks would rather buy bills during the primary auction on Monday, traders said.
A Reuter poll of six institutions showed offer rates of 10.65 to 10.725 percent for the three-month bills; 11.0 to 11.05 for the six months; and 11.30 to 11.375 for the one year.
